ap_chemistry-f01.title: Buffer pH, addition of strong acid and buffer composition

stimulus.description: A student prepares $1.00\text{ L}$ of a buffer that contains $0.4\text{ mol}$ of the weak acid ammonium, NH4⁺ and $0.1\text{ mol}$ of its conjugate base. The pK_a of the weak acid is 9.25 at 25 °C. Assume that adding substances does not change the volume.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Write the Henderson–Hasselbalch equation for this buffer and calculate its pH.

rubric_rows.criterion: Writes pH = pK_a + log([A⁻]/[HA]) with the base in the numerator
common_errors: inverts the ratio

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the pH (about 8.65)
common_errors: uses the pK_a as the pH

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: A student adds $0.03\text{ mol}$ of a strong acid to the buffer. Calculate the pH after the addition.
parts.model_answer: The strong acid converts A⁻ to HA: A⁻ = 0.07 mol, HA = 0.43 mol; pH = 9.25 + log(0.07/0.43) = 8.46.

rubric_rows.criterion: Subtracts the added acid from the moles of A⁻ (0.07 mol)
common_errors: adds the strong acid to A⁻

rubric_rows.criterion: Adds the added acid to the moles of HA (0.43 mol)
common_errors: subtracts it from HA

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the new pH (about 8.46)
common_errors: ignores the added acid

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: A second buffer is made with $0.4\text{ mol}$ of the weak acid in $1.00\text{ L}$. How many moles of the conjugate base must be present for the pH to be 0.70 units above the pK_a?

rubric_rows.criterion: Finds the ratio of base to acid, 10^0.70 (about 5.01)
common_errors: uses the ratio equal to the pH difference

rubric_rows.criterion: Multiplies by the moles of acid to get about 2.005 mol
common_errors: divides by the moles of acid

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Explain, in terms of the species present, how the original buffer resists a change in pH when a small amount of strong acid is added.
parts.model_answer: The conjugate base A⁻ reacts with the added H⁺ to form HA, so the amount of H⁺ that remains free is small and the ratio [A⁻]/[HA] changes only a little.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the conjugate base A⁻ as the species that reacts with the added H⁺ to form the weak acid
common_errors: says the weak acid reacts with the added acid

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies that the ratio [A⁻]/[HA] changes only slightly, so the pH changes only slightly, because both components are present in large amounts compared with the added acid
common_errors: says the added acid is removed from the solution entirely

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: The original buffer is diluted with water to ten times its volume. Does the pH change? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: The pH does not change, because the ratio [A⁻]/[HA] is unchanged by dilution; the buffer capacity decreases.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the pH is unchanged and justifies it with the unchanged ratio of the concentrations of A⁻ and HA
common_errors: says the pH rises because there is more water

ap_chemistry-f02.title: Solubility product, precipitation and the common-ion effect

stimulus.description: The solubility-product constant of $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_{2}}$ at 25 °C is $K_{sp} = 5.6 × 10⁻¹²$. Part (b) concerns mixing equal volumes of a $3.0 × 10⁻⁷\text{ M}$ solution that contains Mg²⁺ and a $2.0 × 10⁻⁷\text{ M}$ solution that contains OH⁻. Part (c) concerns a saturated solution of $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_{2}}$ in a solution that contains $0.02\text{ M}$ of OH⁻ from a soluble salt.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Write the K_sp expression for $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_{2}}$ and calculate its molar solubility in pure water.
parts.model_answer: K_sp = [Mg²⁺]^1[OH⁻]^2; with s mol/L dissolved, (1s)^1(2s)^2 = K_sp, so s = 1.12 × 10⁻⁴ M.

rubric_rows.criterion: Writes K_sp = [Mg²⁺]^1[OH⁻]^2 with the coefficients as exponents
common_errors: includes the solid in the expression

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the molar solubility (about 1.1 × 10⁻⁴ M)
common_errors: takes s equal to K_sp

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the reaction quotient Q immediately after the two solutions are mixed, and state whether a precipitate forms.
parts.model_answer: After mixing, each concentration is halved: [Mg²⁺] = 1.5 × 10⁻⁷ M and [OH⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ M. Q = 1.5 × 10⁻²¹, which is less than K_sp, so no precipitate forms.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the concentrations are halved on mixing equal volumes
common_errors: uses the unmixed concentrations

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates Q (about 1.5 × 10⁻²¹) from the diluted concentrations
common_errors: omits the exponents

rubric_rows.criterion: Compares Q with K_sp and concludes that no precipitate forms
common_errors: reverses the comparison

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Calculate the molar solubility of $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_{2}}$ in the solution that contains $0.02\text{ M}$ of OH⁻.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets up K_sp with [OH⁻] equal to the common-ion concentration (0.02 M) and ignores the small amount that dissolves
common_errors: uses the same concentration for the two ions

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the molar solubility (about 1.4 × 10⁻⁸ M)
common_errors: forgets the exponent of the common ion

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Compare the solubility in part (c) with the solubility in part (a). Justify your answer in terms of equilibrium.
parts.model_answer: The solubility is lower in the solution with the common ion: the added ion shifts the dissolution equilibrium toward the solid (Le Châtelier), so less of the salt dissolves.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the solubility is lower in the solution that contains the common ion
common_errors: says the solubility is greater

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies with the shift of the dissolution equilibrium toward the solid when the concentration of the common ion is increased (or Q greater than K_sp for the pure-water saturation)
common_errors: says that K_sp becomes smaller

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: A student states that adding the soluble salt changes the value of K_sp. Is the statement correct? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: The statement is incorrect: K_sp depends only on temperature, and the added ion changes the concentrations, not the constant.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the statement is incorrect and justifies that K_sp is a constant at a given temperature
common_errors: says K_sp changes with the concentration

stimulus.description: A student dissolves $5.55\text{ g}$ of $\mathrm{MgCl_{2}}$ (molar mass $95.21\text{ g/mol}$) in water to make $500\text{ mL}$ of solution. The student then dilutes the solution with water to a final volume of $2500\text{ mL}$.

ap_chemistry-f07.title: pH of strong acids and bases, and neutralization

stimulus.description: A student has a $0.02\text{ M}$ solution of the strong acid HNO₃ and a $0.025\text{ M}$ solution of the strong base Ba(OH)₂. Both are at 25 °C.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate the pH of the HNO₃ solution.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates pH = 1.70
common_errors: gives the pOH

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the pH of the Ba(OH)₂ solution.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates [OH⁻] = 0.05 M and pH = 12.70
common_errors: ignores the number of hydroxide ions per formula unit

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of the base solution, in mL, needed to neutralize $25\text{ mL}$ of the acid solution.
parts.model_answer: n(H⁺) = 0.00050 mol and each mole of Ba(OH)₂ gives 2 mol OH⁻, so V = 10.0 mL.

rubric_rows.criterion: Equates moles of H⁺ and OH⁻ to find the volume (about 10.0 mL)
common_errors: omits the factor for the number of hydroxide ions

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: What is the pH of the solution at the equivalence point? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: The pH is 7: the ions that remain (a cation of a strong base and the nitrate ion) do not react with water, so the solution is neutral.

rubric_rows.criterion: States pH = 7 and justifies that neither remaining ion is a conjugate of a weak acid or base, so none reacts with water
common_errors: says the pH is below 7 because an acid was used
